canonical_question: Does the 'small-scale SEM-images' from Zhang et al. suggest that the homogeneity of the W-Mo-Nb-Ta alloy was never fully verified at the microstructural level?

question_variants.question: Does the 'small-scale SEM-images' from Zhang et al. suggest that the homogeneity of the W-Mo-Nb-Ta alloy was never fully verified at the microstructural level?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text confirms that only small-scale SEM-images were shown, which implies a lack of extensive verification at the microstructural level in the cited work by Zhang et al.

answers.answer: The evidence indicates that the work by Zhang et al. is limited to showing only small-scale SEM-images and basic corrosion resistance measurements, suggesting limited microstructural verification.
answers.processing_state: as reported by Zhang et al.
answers.mechanism: limited imaging scale restricts homogeneity verification
evidence_spans: the feasibility of laser-based additive manufacturing of the refractory metal high entropy alloy W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 by laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M) is investigated in the present work.
In-situ alloy formation from mixtures of easily available elemental powders is employed

It is shown that PBF-LB/M of W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 is in general possible and that a complete fusion of the powder mixture without a significant number of undissolved particles is achievable by in-situ alloy formation during PBF-LB/M when selecting favorable process parameter combinations.
